title: {{NAME}} and the Kingdom Cup
moral: When you play for something bigger than yourself, you find strength you didn't know you had.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a golden soccer jersey with a crown emblem, dark green shorts, and golden cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The Kingdom Cup was played every five years: one team from each region of the realm, a tournament that mattered more than most things to most people.

{{NAME}}'s team, the Valley Side, had never won.

Their new coach: Princess Cassia, who had played professionally before her coronation, and who arrived at the first training session with a notebook and two surprises.

Surprise one: a conditioning programme that made grown adults cry.

Surprise two: Finn, a border collie who was the best assistant coach anyone had ever seen.

pages.content:
Finn had an ability no human coach could match: he could read a team's movement patterns in real time and bark exactly once when a player was in the wrong position.

One bark: adjust left. Two barks: adjust right. Three: come back.

The team learned Finn's system in two days.

With Finn on the sideline, their defensive structure became extraordinary: always correctly spaced, always in relation to the whole shape.

"How does the dog know that?" asked one player.

"He was trained for sheep," said Princess Cassia. "The principle is the same."

pages.content:
The tournament came. Three matches in three days.

In the second match, down two goals at half time, Princess Cassia made one change: she told {{NAME}} to play further forward and trust Finn to cover the space he left.

{{NAME}} had never played that far forward before.

But Finn barked once (go), so he went.

Two goals in the second half. Three-two.

Afterward, he crouched down and put his hands on Finn's head.

"Thank you," he said.

Finn licked his nose, which he took as professional acknowledgement.

pages.content:
The final: close, hard, decided in the last five minutes.

{{NAME}} scored the winner from a position he never would have been in before: high up the pitch, arriving late, making a run Finn had called with a single sharp bark two seconds earlier.

The ball went in.

He ran toward the sideline and the whole team ran with him, and Finn ran with all of them, barking continuously, which the referee allowed because the match was over.

Princess Cassia stood in the middle of the pitch and watched her team celebrate with complete satisfaction.

pages.content:
He walked home with the medal and the memory of the winning goal in perfect order.

At the park gate, Finn sat beside Princess Cassia watching him leave.

Finn barked once.

{{NAME}} stopped. Turned around. "That means adjust left," he said.

"That means come back next season," said Princess Cassia.

He walked home smiling so hard his face hurt.

In bed, he lay with the medal on the pillow and closed his eyes, and heard it: Finn's bark in the last minute, and the crowd, and the ball going in.
